script:
Li Cheng
Li Cheng was from the Li family of the Eastern Territory. In the year 1499 of the Yuan Calendar, Zhao Zhongzheng, the eldest son of the Zhao family from the Western Gate, approached the Li family requesting cooperation. The Western Gate and Eastern Territory had been mortal enemies for generations, and both families were leading clans of significant influence in their respective regions, making cooperation seemingly impossible. But somehow Zhao Zhongzheng managed to convince the family to agree. However, the family remained suspicious of Zhao Zhongzheng, so they sent Li Cheng to infiltrate.
Li Cheng knew that directly approaching Zhao Zhongzheng would arouse suspicion. After some investigation, he learned that Zhao Zhongzheng had a younger brother named Zhao Zhongyang. So he first found work in the Zhao household and, with his exceptional abilities, quickly gained Zhao Zhongyang's trust, becoming his direct subordinate. Later, Li Cheng found a poor family, gave them money to pretend to be his relatives, then deliberately exposed a weakness to Zhao Zhongzheng, allowing Zhao Zhongzheng to "control" his "family." Zhao Zhongzheng believed this ruse and used it to threaten Li Cheng, giving Li Cheng the opportunity to formally begin approaching Zhao Zhongzheng.
However, Zhao Zhongzheng showed nothing particularly suspicious—he appeared to be nothing more than a profit-seeking merchant. What drew Li Cheng's attention instead was Zhao Zhongyang. Having grown up as a servant's child in the Li household without much care, and with Eastern Territory people valuing profit above all, Li Cheng was moved by Zhao Zhongyang's righteousness and generosity typical of Western Gate people. Zhao Zhongyang even personally cared for him when he fell ill. Despite the Zhao family's power making Zhao Zhongyang an influential figure in the Western Gate, he treated Li Cheng with such kindness that Li Cheng felt genuine warmth and gradually developed true loyalty to this nominal master.
Li Cheng often stayed by Zhao Zhongyang's side. Zhao Zhongyang had two other subordinates: one was the guard Zhang Wei, a greedy man whom Zhao Zhongyang wasn't very satisfied with; the other was Chen Meier, the unofficially designated young mistress. Li Cheng was good at reading people and always felt that Chen Meier had ulterior motives in following Zhao Zhongyang, sometimes warning Zhao Zhongyang about this.
But Zhao Zhongyang said that given his status in the Western Gate, if someone approached him without any ulterior motives, they would be nothing more than stray cats and dogs on the street. Rather than investigating deeply, it was better to treat everyone as good-natured—that way one could live more freely. Li Cheng thought of his own original purpose in approaching Zhao Zhongyang and felt guilty, so he never brought up the matter again.
In June of 1507, Zhao Zhongzheng approached Li Cheng, demanding that he kill Zhao Zhongyang and threatening him with his "family's" lives. Li Cheng, influenced by Zhao Zhongyang, had developed genuine care for this family of strangers and couldn't let them die in vain even without blood relations. Although Zhao Zhongzheng didn't reveal his purpose, Li Cheng could guess it was related to the clan leader position. He agreed on the surface but decided to secretly protect Zhao Zhongyang's safety while also preserving that family. He knew Zhao Zhongzheng wouldn't put all his eggs in one basket.
During this period, Li Cheng hid in Zhao Zhongyang's courtyard every night to protect his safety. Everything seemed normal except that Chen Meier visited more frequently. Due to clan rules, the two couldn't cohabitate overnight, so Chen Meier would leave when night fell.
[Night of July 25th]
Around 11 PM that night, Chen Meier and Zhao Zhongyang were in the room while Li Cheng was outside. Suddenly, an uninvited guest broke into the courtyard—dressed in black with a mask, clearly up to no good. Li Cheng rushed over and wrestled with him. To avoid being discovered, he endured several punches without making a sound.
When the intruder couldn't win the fight, he pulled out a gleaming dagger and stabbed at Li Cheng, who knocked the dagger away with a slap. Eventually, the intruder fled, and Li Cheng didn't pursue him.
Just as Li Cheng caught his breath, Zhao Zhongyang's scream and Chen Meier's cry suddenly came from inside the room. Then Chen Meier rushed out shouting: "Help! Someone is trying to assassinate the young master! The young master is injured!" Li Cheng noticed that Chen Meier shouted a few times, then suddenly stopped, stood stunned for a moment, then returned to the room and closed the door.
Li Cheng didn't dare rush over immediately, fearing that arriving too quickly would expose his secret presence in the courtyard. So he waited a while before bursting into the room, finding Zhao Zhongyang unconscious with Chen Meier beside him in apparent panic. Zhao Zhongyang was foaming at the mouth with a bloody hole in his hand, and there was a bloodstained crossbow bolt in the wall. Li Cheng checked and found he was still breathing.
Then others rushed in, led by the personal guard Zhang Wei. Zhang Wei examined Zhao Zhongyang and quickly called for a doctor. After Zhang Wei checked the room and outside, when he returned to examine Zhao Zhongyang again, Zhao Zhongyang had already stopped breathing.
